description.value: The study investigated how varying cognitive distraction during anticipation of negative and neutral emotional pictures modulates anticipatory brain activity and subsequent emotion processing.

spans.text: We were interested in the neural mechanisms underlying these regulatory processes when cognitive distraction is varied systematically during the anticipation of emotional events.

We anticipated finding a modulation of the functional coupling between the lateral prefrontal cortex, representing mechanisms of cognitive control, and emotion-processing regions.
We hypothesized that we would find no effect on later emotion processing because of the solely short-term effect of anticipatory cognitive distraction.

spans.text: We hypothesized that activation of emotion-processing regions during anticipation would be attenuated with increasing cognitive load of the distraction task.

description.value: An observational, single-group, within-subject event-related fMRI experiment.

spans.text: The whole session consisted of six pseudoblocks (3 × 2-back, 3 × 0-back) containing 10 trials each

In each of the pseudoblocks five trials involving anticipation and presentation of negative pictures and five trials involving anticipation and presentation of neutral pictures were presented in randomized order.

value: During anticipation a main effect of cognitive load (2-back > 0-back) was found in the bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, bilateral superior frontal cortex, bilateral ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, bilateral inferior parietal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex and striatum.
The fMRI data revealed a strong main effect of cognitive load in a fronto-parietal network commonly activated in studies investigating working memory functions.

spans.text: During anticipation a main effect of cognitive load (2-back > 0-back) was found in the bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex [Brodmann area (BA) 46], bilateral superior frontal cortex (BA 6), bilateral ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (BA 47), bilateral inferior parietal cortex (BA 40), anterior cingulate cortex (BA 8/32) and striatum ( Table 1 ).

value: During picture presentation the main effect of emotion (negative > neutral) was exhibited in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, left ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, bilateral amygdala and occipital, fusiform and superior parietal cortex.
We found strong amygdala activation during the presentation of negative pictures.

spans.text: During picture presentation the main effect of emotion (negative > neutral) was exhibited in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (BA 46), left ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (BA 47), bilateral amygdala and occipital, fusiform and superior parietal cortex ( Table 1 , Fig. 3 ).

value: During anticipation a significant interaction of emotion and load occurred in the anterior rostral part of the MPFC and right amygdala for the contrast negative (0-back > 2-back) > neutral (0-back > 2-back).
Both regions showed lower activity during high compared with low cognitive load in the negative emotional trials.
We demonstrate that cognitive distraction down-regulates the neural effects of negative emotion anticipation in the anterior rostral part of the MPFC and amygdala.

spans.text: During anticipation a significant interaction of emotion and load occurred in the anterior rostral part of the MPFC (BA 10) and right amygdala for the contrast [negative (0-back > 2-back) > neutral (0-back > 2-back) masked inclusive by negative (0-back > 2-back) at P < 0.05] ( Table 1 , Fig. 4 ).
